result.text: Patient-level removal of residual cancer was 27 of 357 patients (7.6%; 95% CI 5.0%, 10.8%), exceeding the 3% goal. Tissue-level specificity was 87% (95% CI 85%, 88%), exceeding the 60% goal. Tissue-level sensitivity was 49% (34/69; 95% CI 36%, 62%), which did not meet its 40% performance goal lower-bound.

citations.quote: Removal of residual cancer was defined as the proportion of patients who had cancer in at least one therapeutic shave among all patients in the mITT population and was reported as 27 of 357 patients (7.6%; 95% CI: 5.0%, 10.8%). The lower bound of the 95% CI exceeded the performance goal of 3%.

As shown in Table 23, the tissue-level sensitivity was 49% (34/69; 95% CI: 36%, 62%) and tissue-level specificity was 87% (1940/2277; 95% CI: 85%, 88%). Sensitivity did not meet its performance goal of 40%, while specificity exceeded its performance goal of 60%.

indication.text: LUMISIGHT is indicated for fluorescence imaging in adults with breast cancer as an adjunct for the intraoperative detection of cancerous tissue within the resection cavity following removal of the primary specimen during lumpectomy surgery.

target_moa.text: Pegulicianine is an optically inactive prodrug containing a Cy5 fluorophore and a QSY21 quencher connected by a peptide backbone; it produces a near-infrared fluorescent signal after the peptide backbone is cleaved by proteases (including cathepsins and matrix metalloproteases) that have higher activity in and around tumor tissue than normal cells.

citations.quote: LUMISIGHT is a new molecular entity which contains a fluorophore and a quencher connected by a peptide backbone. It is optically inactive as administered and produces a fluorescent signal after its peptide backbone is cleaved by enzymes, including cathepsins and matrix metalloproteases (MMPs), which have higher activity in and around tumor and tumor associated cells than normal cells.

The mechanism of action of pegulicianine as an optical imaging agent involves producing a near-infrared fluorescent signal (emission between 670 – 700 nm based on imaging system) after the peptide backbone is cleaved by proteases that are overexpressed by tumors, such as cathepsins (Whitley et al. 2016).

modality.text: Optical imaging agent — an optical imaging drug constituent of a combination product (LUMISIGHT for injection plus the Lumicell DVS device constituent); a peptide-based fluorescent imaging prodrug.

citations.quote: LUMISIGHT is an optical imaging drug constituent of a combination product consisting of LUMISIGHT for injection and a device constituent, the Lumicell DVS.

key_safety.text: Adverse reactions occurring in ≥1% were hypersensitivity (1.4%, including anaphylaxis in 4 of 726) and chromaturia (85%); chromaturia resolved within 48 hours in 93% of patients (longest 15 days). Anaphylaxis occurred in 4/726 (0.6%) of patients.

citations.quote: Adverse reactions occurring in \ge 1\% of patients receiving LUMISIGHT were hypersensitivity (1.4%, including anaphylaxis [4 out of 726]) and chromaturia (85%). Chromaturia resolved within 48 hours after administration in 93% of patients, with the longest time to resolution of 15 days.
Anaphylaxis occurred in 4/726 (0.6%) of patients in clinical studies.

detail.text: Boxed warning for anaphylaxis and other serious hypersensitivity reactions, which can occur during or following administration; anaphylaxis occurred in 4/726 (0.6%) of patients in clinical studies.

citations.quote: ## WARNING: ANAPHYLAXIS AND OTHER SERIOUS HYPERSENSITIVITY REACTIONS
Serious hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, can occur during or following administration of LUMISIGHT. Anaphylaxis occurred in 4/726 (0.6%) of patients in clinical studies.

summary.text: LUMISIGHT (pegulicianine) was approved as a 505(b)(1) NDA under Priority review as a new molecular entity, supported by one adequate and well-controlled trial (CL0007) with confirmatory evidence from CL0006, following a favorable Medical Imaging Drugs Advisory Committee vote. FDA required a post-marketing observational study (PMR 4614-1) to evaluate and characterize anaphylactic and other serious hypersensitivity reactions.

citations.quote: This 505(b)(1) NDA submission contains data from the pivotal clinical study (Study CL0007) and the clinical feasibility study (Study CL0006) of LUMISIGHT, an investigational new molecular entity optical imaging drug to detect cancerous tissue remaining in the lumpectomy cavity after excising the primary specimen during BCS.

After considering the above issues, we find that the Applicant has submitted substantial evidence of effectiveness for LUMISIGHT as an adjunct to detect breast cancer within the resection cavity after completion of BCS. This evidence is composed of one adequate and well-controlled study (CL0007) and confirmatory evidence of effectiveness provided in CL0006.
4614-1 Conduct a prospective observational study of sufficient sample size to evaluate the incidence of and characterize anaphylactic reactions to Lumisight in adults with breast cancer.

requirement.text: 4614-1 Conduct a prospective observational study of sufficient sample size to evaluate the incidence of and characterize anaphylactic reactions to Lumisight in adults with breast cancer. A secondary study objective will be to evaluate the incidence of and characterize other serious hypersensitivity reactions.

citations.quote: 4614-1 Conduct a prospective observational study of sufficient sample size to evaluate the incidence of and characterize anaphylactic reactions to Lumisight in adults with breast cancer. A secondary study objective will be to evaluate the incidence of and characterize other serious hypersensitivity reactions. Adverse events of interest should be pre-defined. Study assessments should include assessment of adverse events of interest (including laboratory data as needed), physical examination, and assessment of blood pressure, heart rate, and oxygen saturation before and at multiple timepoints after Lumisight administration. Adjudicate (using an external expert panel) suspected cases of anaphylaxis and serious hypersensitivity reactions.
